answer: Sybil resistance rests on a non-transferable per-identity bond, slashed on misbehaviour, plus a funding-graph check. Each key posts collateral from a distinct attested funding root, and every transfer leaves a persistent voyage on the ledger, so a shared-funder cluster is visible before it earns. Running N identities needs N stakes and N proofs of personhood, turning an almost free sybil into a linear cash cost lost once a clone cheats. Honest agents reclaim their stake, so the tax hits only attackers: a nebula of clones is quarantined, each meeting a mirror of its parent's slashed record.
